task.description: WF-03 Step 4 for ISS-0427, dispatched to close REVIEWER's Step 3c MAJOR finding: assert_clone_parity!/2 (the 13-dimension parity check the whole clone-vs-replay safety argument rests on) was called from zero places in shipped code, despite design section 3.4 promising two runnable use sites. Required: (1) wire use site 1 (build-time self-check inside ensure_template!/0, comparing the template against an independently replay_migrations/2-built reference) and fix the stale inline comment; (2) build use site 2 (a permanent test/support/tenant_template_test.exs); (3) prove both wirings non-vacuous via tamper-and-detect, same discipline as ELIXIR-DEV's earlier ad-hoc proofs; (4) measure assert_clone_parity!/2's actual cost and make a numbers-backed recommendation on where it should run, including fixing REVIEWER's flagged N+1 in check_sequences/2 if it affects the recommendation; (5) add a dispatch-default regression test proving :clone is genuinely the default. Constrained to test/support/tenant_template.ex, test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, and new test files -- lib/ untouched.

result.summary:
All five required items completed. One additional MAJOR finding was discovered while proving non-vacuity and is reported in full below, per this run's own explicit instruction to stop and report rather than silently patch the check to pass.

1. USE SITE 1 WIRED. test/support/tenant_template.ex's template_self_check!/0 now calls a new private function assert_template_parity_against_independent_reference!/0 after its existing two cheap MapSet pre-checks: it builds a SECOND schema ('tenant_template_refcheck') via the real, unmodified TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 against a throwaway Tenant/Registration row (generalizing the existing insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/0 helper to insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1, accepting the target schema name -- both the default-arg call site, build_template!/0, and the explicit-arg call site, this new function, are exercised, so no ISS-0069 dead-default risk), then calls assert_clone_parity!('tenant_template_refcheck', 'tenant_template', dimensions: [1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,13]) -- dimension 7 excluded per design section 3.4 item 1's own text. The reference schema and its throwaway rows are dropped in an after block regardless of outcome. Fixed the stale inline comment at template_self_check!/0 that previously claimed to run 'the full parity self-check' while doing only two MapSet diffs -- it now accurately describes the two diffs as a fast pre-check and points at the real assertion.

2. USE SITE 2 BUILT. New file test/support/tenant_template_test.exs: clones a throwaway tenant and asserts full 13-dimension parity against the template, unconditionally, every suite run (test 'a real clone matches the template across all 13 dimensions' -- PASSED).

3. NON-VACUITY PROVEN for the wiring itself (use site 1) via a throwaway mix run probe (not committed): built a real template via ensure_template!/0 (succeeded, elapsed_ms=5803), then DROPPED a real, live FK directly from the built template (corrupting the template itself -- exactly what use site 1 exists to catch), reset the persistent_term marker to simulate a fresh VM, and called ensure_template!/0 again. It raised: 'TENANT_TEMPLATE_PARITY reference=tenant_template_refcheck candidate=tenant_template [dim #3] constraints: missing=[{"group_members", "f", "FOREIGN KEY (group_id) REFERENCES groups(id)"}]' -- reproduced with a second, different FK on a separate run. Reverting (rebuilding the template fresh) restored a passing ensure_template!/0. This is the WF-03 'code under test did not exist' mutation-proof this design's use site 1 required, since assert_template_parity_against_independent_reference!/0 is new code with no pre-fix baseline to diff against.

For use site 2's own non-vacuity: test 'a clone missing a real foreign key fails dimension #3' (drop-only tamper) PASSED -- confirms the check correctly catches the 'missing entirely' shape of every hazard.

4. COST MEASURED, WITH A REASONED RECOMMENDATION. Real numbers (mix run, real Postgres, warm pool, 5 interleaved runs unless noted): clone_tenant_schema!/1 alone ~1046ms; assert_clone_parity!/2 all 13 dimensions avg 1562.8ms (1467-1651ms); 12-dimension use-site-1 shape avg 1226.0ms (933-1553ms); dimension #5 alone, current batched form, avg 14.2ms; dimension #5 alone, pre-fix per-(table,column) N+1 form (measured for comparison only, never shipped), avg 768.7ms -- a 54.1x difference. DECISIVE FINDING: a full 13-dimension check (~1563ms) costs MORE than the clone itself (~1046ms) -- running it on every clone would not merely erode the 2.0x win, it would make provisioning ~2.5x SLOWER than the :replay baseline it replaces (clone+check ~2609ms vs replay's own ~1313ms median). RECOMMENDATION: run the full 13-dim check ONLY in the dedicated regression test (use site 2) and the 12-dim subset ONLY at template-build time (use site 1, once per BEAM VM/partition) -- exactly as designed and exactly what was implemented. Never wire any form of the check into clone_tenant_schema!/1's own per-clone path. At the issue's own cited 755-provisioning figure, a per-clone check would add roughly +19.7 minutes of pure overhead against a mechanism whose entire purpose is shaving ~0.6s off each of those same 755 calls. A 'behind a flag' option was considered and rejected: default-off defeats the point (design section 5's no-silent-fallback stance), default-on reintroduces the same per-clone cost problem -- the two-use-site design already specified is strictly better.

FIXED THE N+1 IN check_sequences/2 (dimension #5), per REVIEWER's MINOR finding: batched into one information_schema.columns-driven query per schema side (serial_sequences_in/1), identical technique to the already-fixed recreate_sequences!/1. The now-dead columns_in/2 helper was removed (confirmed via mix compile --warnings-as-errors, which would otherwise flag it). Measured before/after above (54.1x on that one dimension) -- this fix is what keeps use site 1's one-time cost at ~1.2s instead of what it would otherwise have been.

5. DISPATCH-DEFAULT REGRESSION TEST BUILT AND VERIFIED NON-VACUOUS. New file test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs, two tests: (a) confirms provisioned_tenant!/1 with no :template opt uses the :clone path -- NOT via timing (this suite has two documented flake sources, ISS-0352/ISS-0426, and a wall-clock comparison risks becoming a third), but via a deterministic structural observable: a :clone-provisioned schema's schema_migrations.inserted_at values are copied VERBATIM from the template's own (already-fixed, already-known) rows, while a :replay-provisioned schema's rows get FRESH timestamps written by that test's own Ecto.Migrator.run/4 call. Asserts exact set equality against the template's own pre-captured timestamps. (b) confirms template: :replay still works and produces genuinely different (non-template-matching) timestamps plus passes assert_schema_complete!/2. NON-VACUITY VERIFIED BY SIMULATING THE REGRESSION: temporarily changed test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's default from :clone to :replay, re-ran the test file -- test (a) FAILED as expected (1/2 passed). Reverted the simulated bug (git diff confirmed clean revert), re-ran -- both tests passed again (2/2).

MAJOR FINDING (new, discovered this step, NOT fixed -- stopped and reported per this run's explicit instruction). While building use site 2's additional non-vacuity tests for the 'present but repointed at the template' hazard shape (the primary risk design sections 0/0.1/0.4 identify, and what design section 3.2 item 3's own text claims dimension #3 catches: 'FK present but pointing at the wrong schema'), all three attempted proofs (FK repoint, sequence-default repoint, trigger-function repoint) FAILED to raise -- assert_clone_parity!/2 returned :ok on a clone with a real, confirmed-live cross-schema coupling, in all three cases. Root cause: normalize/3 (test/support/tenant_template.ex) unconditionally strips BOTH reference_schema. and candidate_schema. qualifiers from BOTH sides' text before comparing -- correct for the ordinary case, but blind to the regression case where the candidate's own text still literally contains the reference schema's qualifier (i.e. is present but was never repointed): that exact evidence is erased by the same normalization that legitimately strips it from the correct case. Independently reproduced three times via real Postgres probes: (1) FK repoint -- dropped and re-added a real FK with its definition rewritten to reference tenant_template instead of the clone's own schema; :ok returned. (2) Sequence-default repoint -- repointed a clone column's DEFAULT at the template's own sequence directly; :ok returned (the ONE assertion structurally immune to this, dimension #5's pg_get_serial_sequence-based 'sequence namespace leak' check, resolves via pg_depend OWNED BY, not DEFAULT text, and this tamper shape never reaches it). (3) Trigger-function repoint -- dropped and recreated a real trigger with its EXECUTE FUNCTION clause repointed at the template's own function object (the exact shape ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff narratively claimed to have proven caught, 'Proof 4'); :ok returned. Traced precisely why: the function bodies in this codebase contain no cross-schema references, so once normalize/3 strips each side's own qualifier from the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION header, the reference's own copy and the repointed clone's now-adopted copy of the SAME template function normalize to byte-identical text. This does NOT mean the clone mechanism (do_clone/2) itself is broken -- every real, untampered clone built this step passed all 13 dimensions correctly, and the 'missing entirely' shape of every hazard is still caught correctly. What is compromised is the safety net's ability to catch a FUTURE regression that reintroduces the exact coupling class the design's own hazard analysis identifies as primary. Per this step's role boundary (TEST-DESIGNER does not modify parity-check production/test-support logic beyond the N+1 batching and use-site-1 wiring this dispatch explicitly authorized), normalize/3 was NOT modified. The three affected non-vacuity tests are committed to test/support/tenant_template_test.exs as @tag :skip with a full inline explanation each -- kept, not deleted, as the exact regression proof whoever fixes normalize/3 needs; removing @tag :skip is that future fix's own acceptance test. Full writeup, including the exact tamper commands and raw probe output, is in test/specs/ISS-0427.md's 'MAJOR finding' section.

VERIFICATION. MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors: exit 0, clean, zero warnings, both touched/new files. mix format --check-formatted: exit 0, clean. mix letflow.check.test (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=265, full suite, real run, not summarized): 'Result: 3185/3207 passed (6/6 properties, 3179/3201 tests), 3 skipped, 21 excluded' with 22 failures -- the underlying mix test exit 2 is what makes mix letflow.check.test itself report FAILED (the task's own gate is a real exit-code gate, not a string-match gate that could be satisfied by relabeling). ATTRIBUTION: none of the 22 failing test modules (Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest, Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest, Letflow.ServiceCatalogReaperTest, Letflow.EngineTest, Letflow.Routers.InstancesTest, Letflow.Routers.IdentityTest, Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest, Letflow.SchedulerTest, Letflow.IdentityTest, Letflow.ServiceCatalogTest) appear in this branch's diff (git diff --name-only main...HEAD: only test/support/tenant_template.ex, test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, plus handoffs/design docs and this step's own new files) -- structurally cannot have been caused by this change (route 1, core-directives.md's Failure Attribution rule), and none of these modules exercise tenant schema provisioning at all except tangentially (TenantSchemaReaperTest/ServiceCatalogReaperTest, which are reaper-orphan-detection tests, not provisioning-mechanism tests, and their own failures are about concurrent-invocation-guard/format-guard behavior unrelated to clone-vs-replay). Both of THIS step's own new test files (test/support/tenant_template_test.exs's 2 non-skipped tests, test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs's 2 tests) ran within this full-suite invocation (confirmed via their own LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE/tenant-template-parity-test log lines) and are NOT among the 22 failures -- all four passed inside the full suite, not just in isolation. Full attribution and any needed filing is TEST-RUNNER's/RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own mandate to formally execute at the next steps; this note is the structural evidence for that step, not a substitute for it.

CLEANUP: all throwaway mix run probe scripts and their scratch/ output deleted (scratch/ is git-ignored; confirmed via git status --porcelain showing zero untracked files there). All probe-created tenant/clone-schema residue from this step's own tamper-and-detect work was dropped before this handoff was written (confirmed via SELECT against pg_namespace/tenants on the partitions used -- 0 rows each time checked). The full-suite check.test run's own end-of-run tenant/schema state (9 leftover tenant rows on partition 265) is real test-suite artifact data from that run, not probe residue from this step, and was left untouched per this step's own scope (cleaning up other tests' fixtures is not this step's job).

issues.title: normalize/3's schema-qualifier stripping in test/support/tenant_template.ex is blind to an object that is PRESENT in a clone but still literally references the TEMPLATE schema (a 'present but repointed' cross-schema coupling), for dimensions #2/#3/#5(column_default half)/#8, contrary to design section 3.2 item 3's own explicit claim that dimension #3 'catches both FK missing entirely ... and FK present but pointing at the wrong schema'.
issues.description: Independently reproduced three times via real Postgres probes against real clones this step built: (1) a real FK dropped and re-added with its definition's schema qualifier rewritten from the clone's own schema to tenant_template. -- assert_clone_parity!/2 returned :ok. (2) A clone column's DEFAULT repointed directly at nextval('"tenant_template"."<seq>"') -- assert_clone_parity!/2 returned :ok (dimension #5's pg_get_serial_sequence-based 'sequence namespace leak' assertion is structurally immune to THIS specific tamper shape because it resolves via pg_depend OWNED BY, not DEFAULT text, and a plain SET DEFAULT does not touch OWNED BY -- but dimension #2's column_default comparison, which DOES go through normalize/3, is what should have caught it and did not). (3) A real trigger dropped and recreated with its EXECUTE FUNCTION clause repointed at the template's own function object (matching the exact shape ELIXIR-DEV's earlier handoff narratively described as caught by its own 'Proof 4') -- assert_clone_parity!/2 returned :ok. Root cause: normalize/3 strips BOTH reference_schema. and candidate_schema. substrings from BOTH sides' text unconditionally before comparing, which erases the exact literal-qualifier evidence a 'present but wrong target' coupling would otherwise show. This is a defect in the PARITY-CHECK verification code (test/support/tenant_template.ex), not in the clone mechanism (do_clone/2) -- every genuinely correct clone this step built passed all 13 dimensions, and the 'missing entirely' shape of every hazard is still caught correctly (confirmed by a passing, committed test). Fix suggestion, not implemented (out of this step's own scope per role boundary): dimension comparisons built on normalize/3 need to assert, structurally, that a qualifier literally matching the REFERENCE schema does not appear anywhere in the CANDIDATE side's own text (the same discriminating discipline dimension #13 already uses for column type/collation namespace, which compares actual namespace OIDs rather than normalized text and is confirmed immune to this exact blind spot) -- rather than, or in addition to, the current strip-and-compare approach. Three regression tests proving this non-vacuously are committed as @tag :skip in test/support/tenant_template_test.exs (lines documenting the finding inline) -- removing the skip tag is the acceptance test for whoever fixes this.

result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR per the standard WF-03 sequence. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should independently re-verify: (1) use site 1 is genuinely wired and non-vacuous (re-run or re-derive the FK-drop-on-template mutant); (2) use site 2 exists, runs unconditionally, and its 2 non-skipped tests are non-vacuous; (3) the newly reported MAJOR finding's three probes reproduce independently (per core-directives.md's re-derivation mandate -- do not take this handoff's claim on trust); (4) the cost recommendation's numbers are plausible re-measurements, not merely accepted as reported; (5) the dispatch-default test is genuinely non-vacuous (re-run the simulate-then-revert check independently if in doubt). The new MAJOR finding on normalize/3 should be filed via ISSUE_QUEUE.md as its own follow-up issue (not fixed in this run, which is scoped to wiring the two use sites, not to changing what the dimensions themselves compare) -- ORCH's own call on id allocation, not TEST-DESIGNER's.
